patch.value: GH-1618: prevent automated comment churn from misleading next-work priority

**Version:** pm 2026.10.28, a real tracker with 112 next candidates (90 ready). `pm next --help` says: *"Answers 'what should I work on now?' with the highest-priority ready item"*.

**Observed:** the recommendation is a **P2** task, an append-only automation audit log ("Hosted auto-update runs … Never close this item"). A host cron appends one comment to it every hour; it has 161 comments. Two **P0** issues, both open, unblocked and unassigned, rank 9th and 17th, behind six P1 items.

`pm next --json --explain-ranking` shows why:

| id | priority | baseline_rank | final rank | recency | activity_density | priority_pressure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| audit-log task | P2 | 35 | **1** | 0.342 (hourly `comment_add`, classed `substantive`) | **0.25** | 0.175 |
| P1 feature | P1 | 11 | 2 | 0.291 | 0.030 | 0.262 |
| P0 issue | P0 | — | 9 | — | — | — |

`recency` takes its coordinate from the latest `comment_add`, classed `event_class: substantive`. `activity_density` counts comments. So machine-written log comments outweigh priority, and a P0 incident loses to a log that grows by itself.

**Why it matters for agents:** an agent that follows `pm next` (the documented "what now?" entry point) works on the wrong item and never gets to the P0 work. It also costs a second query and manual re-ranking to notice. Any tracker with an automation that comments regularly (CI receipts, updater runs, sync bots) has the same problem.

**Expected (any of these would fix it):**
1. Treat priority as a floor: a ready P0 always ranks above ready P1/P2 unless a caller-declared intent says otherwise. The help text promises this.
2. Don't count automated or append-only comment churn as substantive recency or activity. For example, classify comments by `author_source` / harness, or let an item be declared non-actionable/log so it never becomes `recommended`.
3. In the default (non-explain) output, give the reason a lower-priority item outranks a higher-priority one (`reasons` currently shows just `p2`), so an agent can see why the recommendation isn't the highest priority.

Related: #513 (ready queue not priority-ordered, closed). This is the scorer variant of it: the queue is now ranked, but by signals that automation can inflate.


Intake only: reproduce against the current public SDK before selecting a ranking policy. Preserve custom project scoring and explicit intent while reconciling the default recommendation with its documented priority contract.

Reproduce a ready P0 population competing with automated P2 comment churn;Define explicit default and caller-customizable ranking policy;Verify explanations and SDK CLI MCP parity with bounded token costs
Default next-work advice cannot silently elevate an automated P2 log above ready P0 work; documented policy and ranking explanations match tested behavior.
